page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top. Page number at the top right. Gathering signature at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: ANGLORVM lingua mixta est ex multis. Hoc norunt ejus linguæ, & Gallicæ, & Germanicæ periti. Habitant autem Insulam, in Europa maximam; quæ Albion, Britannia, Anglia, aliter q; dicitur. Albion quidem, ab albis montibus, primùm ad eam navigantibus apparentibus: Britannia verò vel à Bruto, Trojano duce, ex Aquitania illuc trajecto, vel à Britannis, populis Galliæ, Bedâ ipso, qui Anglus fuit, teste: Anglia deniq;, vel ab Angelâ, Saxonum reginâ, quæ expulsis gigantibus, eam tunc incolentibus, inter suos Insulam partiens, ut victoriæ gentisq; memoria nunquam intercideret, Angliam illam vocavit: vel ab Angilis ejusdem Saxoniæ populis, quos, quum à Pictis Scotisq; molestiâ afficerentur, Britanni in auxilium vocârunt, atq; hinc tandem terræ bonitate & amœnitate allecti eos circumdederunt, ac Insulanorum bona inter se partiti sunt. quanquam Angilos Suevos, non Saxones fuisse auctor est Ptolemæus. Vel dicta est quasi Anguli terra, seu nostri Orbis Angulus Goropius Becanus in originibus Atuaticis Anglos dictos vult à magna potentia navali, quasi Angel[?]/ quæ vox hamos piscatorios significat.

page.notes: The brackets after "ex multis", "ARABVM" and the small mark at the foot left are printer's marks and are left out. The word after "quasi" is in black letter and was read as "Angel" with a doubtful final letter; the Greek-looking first letter is uncertain. The paragraph "ARABVM" continues on the next page. The bottom-left small marks are stains and not text. The signature "M 5" is set at the foot right.
